metadata.title: Symptomatic Nonerosive Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease: Developing Drugs for Treatment: Draft Guidance for Industry
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

candidates.context: Sponsors developing drugs for the treatment of sGERD should consider the following: 117 • Sponsors should consider a treatment period of at least 8 to 12 weeks to assess the drug’s 124 benefit for the treatment of sGERD. The trial duration and timing of efficacy assessments 125 should be guided by the mechanism of action of the drug, its expected onset of action, 126 and the time frame in which a clinical benefit is expected to be observed in the intended 127 population. Additionally, sponsors should consider the duration of exposure necessary to 128 inform the safety profile of the drug for its intended use and durability of treatment effect. 129

candidates.statement: • Trials should assess a primary efficacy endpoint of the proportion of heartburn-free days 145 during the prespecified assessment period, where a heartburn-free day is defined as a 24- 146 hour period with no heartburn, to establish efficacy for the relief of heartburn associated 147 with sGERD. 148

candidates.context: D. Safety Considerations 210 • Multiple potential risks have been identified with long-term acid suppression (e.g., 214 Clostridioides difficile enteric infections, osteoporosis-related bone fractures, vitamin 215 deficiencies). Sponsors should consider these potential risks, as well as known adverse 216 events associated with the therapeutic class of the drug, to inform the overall extent and 217 duration of treatment provided in the program’s overall safety database. 218
